overall_summary: Bitcoin held firm above eighty-four thousand with strong ETF inflows, showing resilience through the yield spike. Macro headwinds from soft sentiment, a firm dollar, and inflation warnings plus energy-related geopolitical risks keep the tone mixed. A heavy data slate of PCE, GDP, and payrolls leaves the next move dependent on upcoming prints.
key_points: Soft sentiment, firm dollar, inflation caution
US-China tariff cuts support risk tone
Energy geopolitics keep gas and oil tense
PCE, GDP, payrolls drive the week ahead

items.title: Bitget Hack Losses Revised to $387.5 Million
items.summary: Bitget raised its estimate of the September 24 hot and warm wallet breach to three hundred eighty-seven point five million dollars after fuller accounting of Zcash and Tron assets. Attackers spoofed backend transfer data rather than stealing keys; cold wallets stayed safe and the exchange's protection fund exceeds four hundred sixty-four million to cover customers. North Korea links are suspected but unconfirmed, some stablecoins were frozen, a recovery bounty is live, and staged withdrawals restart around September 28. Traders should watch for any confidence hit to centralized exchanges even though the market largely shrugged it off so far.
items.impact: Contained CEX risk; limited immediate BTC pressure if fund covers fully

items.title: Bitcoin ETFs Pull In $2.39 Billion for the Week
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded net inflows every day of the September 21-25 week totaling about two point three nine billion dollars, led by BlackRock's IBIT. Daily prints slowed from nearly one billion earlier to roughly one hundred thirty-five to one hundred ninety million later in the week, yet the streak extended and helped erase earlier 2026 deficits. Bitcoin is consolidating near eighty-four thousand after touching eighty-seven thousand. Persistent institutional buying remains a key demand floor for traders watching whether the bid continues into next week.
items.impact: Supports price floor and reduces downside from profit-taking

items.title: Bitcoin Holds $84K Through Treasury Yield Shock
items.summary: Bitcoin stayed near eighty-four thousand even as the ten-year Treasury yield hit multi-decade highs around five point two percent and longer yields spiked further. Derivatives open interest across major exchanges dropped about one point seven billion dollars or fourteen percent while price fell only roughly two percent from recent highs. Long liquidations hit in the low hundreds of millions. The resilience and forced deleveraging matter because they clean the book and show spot demand absorbing macro pressure without a cascade.
items.impact: Deleveraging reduces cascade risk; holds key support zone

items.title: SEC Crypto Mom Hester Peirce Exits October 2
items.summary: Commissioner Hester Peirce, long nicknamed Crypto Mom for her pro-clarity stance, submitted her resignation effective October 2 after nearly nine years. She heads to Regent University law school; the move leaves the SEC with only two sitting commissioners and no named successor yet. It arrives after the Clarity Act setback and alongside fresh staff crypto FAQs. Traders should note the loss of an internal advocate even under a friendlier chair, as quorum and future nominations could shape enforcement tone.
items.impact: Short-term regulatory uncertainty; limited immediate price catalyst

items.title: Dormant Whale Moves $380 Million in Bitcoin
items.summary: A wallet moved nearly forty-five hundred Bitcoin worth about three hundred eighty million dollars in one September 25 transaction. The bulk had sat untouched since April 2022. Coins went to a new unidentified address and remained unspent hours later, so there is no confirmed exchange deposit or sale. Large old-coin awakenings always draw eyes because any later move to venues could add supply; right now it is just a re-custody signal traders will track closely.
items.impact: Watch for any follow-on exchange inflows that could pressure price

items.title: Sequans Sells Final 314 BTC, Ends Treasury Strategy
items.summary: French chipmaker Sequans completed its Bitcoin treasury exit by selling the remaining three hundred fourteen coins, leaving zero crypto on the balance sheet. Earlier sales had already funded convertible debt redemption; management now focuses purely on semiconductors. The move runs opposite corporate buyers still adding. It is small absolute size but another data point of a firm rotating out after using Bitcoin for balance-sheet repair.
items.impact: Minor supply addition; contrasts with ongoing corporate accumulation trend

items.title: Durable Goods Flat but Core Capex Surges 1.6%
items.summary: August durable goods orders came in unchanged, beating expectations for a decline, while the key nondefense capital goods excluding aircraft rose a strong 1.6 percent. Transportation dragged the headline, but underlying business investment looks solid, especially in machinery and tech-related categories. Traders should care because this supports the soft-landing or resilient-growth narrative that keeps the Fed in play for more hikes while also backing corporate spending that can lift risk assets.
items.impact: Supports growth narrative and higher-for-longer rates

items.title: Michigan Sentiment Hits Four-Month Low at 48.1
items.summary: Final University of Michigan consumer sentiment for September printed 48.1, a touch above the preliminary but down sharply from 51.7 in August and near multi-month lows. One-year inflation expectations jumped to 4.6 percent from 4.0 percent, with longer-term also ticking higher. Crypto traders need to watch this because rising household inflation fears reinforce the Fed's hawkish stance and keep pressure on rate-sensitive assets like Bitcoin.
items.impact: Fuels rate-hike bets and dampens risk appetite

items.title: Treasury Yields Hit Multi-Decade Highs Then Ease
items.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield touched levels not seen since 2007 around 5.23 percent earlier before settling near 5.16 to 5.18 percent on Friday, while the 30-year hit highs last seen in 2004. The move came on strong PMI data earlier in the week and hawkish Fed talk, with some relief Friday from softer oil prices. Bond yields this elevated raise discount rates across markets and typically weigh on crypto valuations until the path stabilizes.
items.impact: Higher yields pressure risk assets and Bitcoin

items.title: Fed's Hammack Warns on Inflation Mindset Risk
items.summary: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said Friday that the biggest risk is an inflationary mindset taking hold after years above target, and that the recent bond yield surge reflects real rates and solid growth more than unanchored expectations. She and other officials have kept the door open to further tightening. This keeps markets pricing elevated odds of another hike, which is a headwind for leveraged risk assets including crypto.

items.title: Dollar Holds Near Multi-Week Highs After Rally
items.summary: The DXY dollar index pulled back modestly on Friday to around 101 after hitting eight-week or two-month highs earlier in the week on rising rate-hike expectations and strong data. It remains elevated versus recent levels. A firm dollar often correlates with pressure on Bitcoin and other risk assets as global liquidity conditions tighten in relative terms.
items.impact: Strong dollar typically weighs on crypto

items.title: Big Week Ahead: PCE, GDP, Then Nonfarm Payrolls
items.summary: No major US data today on Saturday, but next week brings the critical August PCE inflation and Q2 GDP third estimate on Wednesday, followed by September nonfarm payrolls on Friday. Markets will parse these for clues on whether the Fed hikes again in October. Crypto traders should position carefully around these prints as they will drive yields, the dollar, and risk sentiment into the next FOMC.
items.impact: High-volatility catalysts for rates and risk assets

items.title: Trump Rejects Iran's 7-Day Hormuz Reopen Plan
items.summary: Iran offered a concrete seven-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and pause regional fighting if the US lifts its naval blockade, eases oil sanctions, and releases frozen assets. Reports say President Trump rejected it and told aides he expects renewed strikes after the November midterms. Traders should care because Hormuz handles a huge share of global oil; prolonged closure or escalation keeps the energy risk premium elevated and fuels inflation fears that hit risk assets hard.
items.impact: Sustains high oil prices and risk-off pressure on crypto and equities

items.title: US-China Agree $30 Billion Reciprocal Tariff Cuts
items.summary: During Xi Jinping's Washington visit, Beijing and Washington reached an eight-point consensus including a thirty-billion-dollar reciprocal tariff reduction, a new trade council, and formal AI risk dialogue. They also extended the prior trade truce. This is market-relevant because lower tariffs ease supply-chain costs and reduce trade-war uncertainty, supporting global growth and risk appetite for assets like Bitcoin.
items.impact: Positive for risk assets via reduced trade friction and growth outlook

items.title: France Deploys Troops to Guard Saudi Yanbu Oil Hub
items.summary: After Houthi missile and drone attacks on Saudi energy sites including Yanbu and claims of strikes near Riyadh, President Macron announced French troops, radars, and defense systems will protect the Red Sea oil terminal. Saudi allies including Pakistan and Turkey reaffirmed their Mecca defense pact. Yanbu is a critical alternative export route while Hormuz stays disrupted, so any further hits threaten oil supply and keep energy prices sticky.
items.impact: Heightens oil-supply risks and supports elevated energy prices

items.title: Ukraine Hits Russian Ilsky Refinery as Strikes Intensify
items.summary: Ukrainian forces struck the Ilsky oil refinery in Russia's Krasnodar region overnight, sparking a fire, while Russia continued drone and missile attacks on Ukraine that killed several civilians and damaged infrastructure including a major steel plant. Zelensky said Trump gave final approval for Ukraine to license production of Patriot missiles. The tit-for-tat energy strikes tighten global fuel supplies and keep European energy markets on edge heading into winter.
items.impact: Adds to refined-product tightness without clear directional catalyst yet

items.title: European Gas Prices Set to Stay Elevated This Winter
items.summary: Goldman Sachs and others warn European gas prices, already up around seventy percent since July, will likely remain high due to ongoing Middle East LNG disruptions through Hormuz and low storage levels. Winter demand could push prices higher still if Persian Gulf exports stay constrained. Elevated energy costs feed into inflation and squeeze European growth, which typically weighs on global risk sentiment including crypto.
items.impact: Supports higher inflation and risk-off flows into winter

items.title: US-Russia Talks Signal Limited Ukraine Energy Ceasefire Interest
items.summary: After meetings at the UN, Secretary of State Rubio said both Ukraine and Russia voiced interest in a limited ceasefire covering grain and energy targets ahead of winter. Russia remains resistant to broader deals while continuing strikes. A narrow pause on energy infrastructure could ease some European supply fears, but lack of progress keeps the war as a lingering drag on sentiment.
items.impact: Unresolved; potential mild relief if limited deal forms, otherwise status quo risk
